source.notes: Every page footer prints 'ISC (CLASS XII) SPECIMEN QUESTION PAPER 2026' (pages 1-9) and 'ISC (CLASS XII) SPECIMEN ANSWER KEY 2026' (pages 10-19), so examYear = 2026 (the examination year the specimen is for); the file was uploaded to cisce.org in 2025/08. The question paper (9 printed pages, PDF pages 1-9) is followed in the same PDF by its answer key (PDF pages 10-19); answerSourceUrl is the same URL. Maximum Marks 70, Time Allotted Three Hours plus fifteen minutes reading time. Section A: Question 1 (A) [4×1], (B) [7×1], (C) [3×1], each sub-part entered separately (14 marks). Section B: Questions 2-11, 2 marks each; Section C: Questions 12-18, 3 marks each; Section D: Questions 19-21, 5 marks each. Internal choice (one question in each of Sections B, C, D): Questions 9, 16 and 21, each entered as two alternatives sharing choiceGroup. Where a Section B-D question has several sub-parts under one bracket mark, it is kept as one entry (marks are not itemised per sub-part on the paper). Counting one alternative per choice group the pack totals 70. Cognitive tags printed per sub-part in brackets (e.g. '(Understanding)') are recorded only when all parts of an entry share one tag. Chemical subscripts are kept flat as in the text layer; powers of ten, unit exponents, ionic charges in the stated data, and degree signs were rebuilt from page renders and flagged.

questions.text:
Read the passage carefully and answer the questions that follow.
Vishal set up an experiment to find the resistance of aqueous KCl solution for different concentrations at 298K using a conductivity cell connected to a Wheatstone bridge. He fed the Wheatstone bridge with A.C. power in the audio frequency range 550 to 5000 cycles per second. Once the resistance was calculated from null point, he also calculated the conductivity (κ) and molar conductivity (Λm) and recorded his readings in tabular form which is given below.
S.No. | Conc. (M) | κ (S cm⁻¹) | Λm (S cm² mol⁻¹)
1. | 1∙00 | 111∙3 × 10⁻³ | 111∙3
2. | 0∙10 | 12∙9 × 10⁻³ | 129∙0
3. | 0∙01 | 1∙41 × 10⁻³ | 141∙0
Why did the molar conductivity increase though the conductivity decreased with dilution?
extractionIssues: Passage shared by Question 1(C)(i)-(iii); reproduced in each entry.
Table on page 4 (conductivity data) given here in linear form from the text layer; check against the PDF.
Notation rebuilt from the PDF layout and page render (powers of ten, unit exponents, degree signs, Λ°m); check against the PDF

officialAnswer.text: The conductivity of a solution is the conductance of ions present in a unit volume of the solution. With dilution, the number of ions per unit volume decreases. Hence, conductivity decreases with dilution. The molar conductance (Λm) is the product of conductivity (κ) and the volume of the solution containing 1 mole of the electrolyte. Λm = κ x Vm. Hence, Λm increases on dilution.

questions.text:
When 2g of benzoic acid (C6H5COOH) is dissolved in 25g of benzene, it shows a depression in freezing point equal to 1∙62 K. Molal depression constant for benzene is 4∙7 K kg mol⁻¹.
What is the percentage association of acid if it forms dimer in solution?
extractionIssues: Subscripts/charges flattened as in the text layer: C6H5COOH.
Notation rebuilt from the PDF layout and page render (powers of ten, unit exponents, degree signs, Λ°m); check against the PDF
Official answer's fractions/equations rebuilt inline from the layout; check against the PDF.
The scheme labels the result 'Degree of dissociation (α)' and prints '1 − 1/h' although the question asks for percentage association of a dimer; reproduced as printed, not corrected.

officialAnswer.text: Given; wt. of solute = 2.0g, wt. of solvent = 25g, ΔTf = 1.62 K, kf = 4.7 K kg mol⁻¹, Mnormal = 122 g mol⁻¹. mobs = (1000 x kf.w)/(ΔTf x w) = (1000 x 4.7 x 2)/(1.62 x 25) = 241.98 g mol⁻¹. i = Normal mol. wt/observed mol. wt = 122.0/241.98 or = 0.504. Degree of dissociation (α) = (1 − i)/(1 − 1/h) = (1 − 0.504)/(1 − 1/2) = 0.496/(1/2). (α) = 0.496 x 2 = 0.992 = 99.2%

(Given: E°(Cu²⁺/Cu) = +0∙34V, E°(Ag⁺/Ag) = +0∙80V)
(c) Two metals A and B have standard reduction potential values -2∙37V and +0∙80V respectively. Which of these will liberate H2 gas from dil. HCl.?
extractionIssues: Internal choice: alternative (i) of Question 16 (OR (ii)).

officialAnswer.text: (a) Upon dilution the specific conductivity will decrease, and molar conductivity will increase. (b) The following reaction takes place: Cu + 2Ag⁺(aq.) → Cu²⁺(aq.) + 2Ag; E°cell = E°cathode + E°anode = + 0.80 – (+ 0.34); E°cell = + 0.46. questions.text:
(a) Calculate the values of Ecell and ΔG for the following cell reaction at 25°C:
Zn(s)/Zn²⁺(0.0004M) || Cd²⁺(0.2M)/Cd(s)
(Given; E°(Zn²⁺/Zn) = -0∙763V; E°(Cd²⁺/Cd) = -0∙403V
1 Faraday = 96,500 coulombs, R = 8∙314 JK⁻¹ mol⁻¹)
(b) Calculate how long it will take to deposit 1∙0 g of chromium when a current of 1∙25 ampere flows through a solution of chromium (III) sulphate.
(Atomic weight of Cr = 52, 1 Faraday = 96,500 coulombs.)
extractionIssues: Internal choice: alternative (ii) of Question 16 (OR (i)).
Subscripts, charges and exponents in the cell notation and the Nernst working rebuilt from the page render; check against the PDF.
Official answer's fractions/equations rebuilt inline from the layout; check against the PDF.
The answer's 'Given' line (restating the cell) is omitted as it only repeats the question.

officialAnswer.text: (a) Cell reaction: Zn(s) + Cd²⁺(aq.) → Zn²⁺(aq.) + Cd(s); E°cell = E°cathode – E°anode = -0.403V – (-0.763V) = 0.36V; Ecell = E°cell – (0.059/2) log [Zn²⁺]/[Cd²⁺] = 0.36 – (0.059/2) log [0.0004]/[0.2] = 0.36 – (0.059/2) log 2 x 10⁻³ = 0.36 – (0.059/2)(−2.6990) = 0.36 + 0.08 = 0.44V; Ecell = + 0.44V; ΔG = – nFE or = – 2 x 96500 x 0.44; ΔG = – 84920 J or – 84.92 kJ (b) Cr³⁺ + 3e⁻ → Cr; 52g of chromium requires current = 3 x 96,500 coulombs or 1g of chromium requires current = (3 x 96500 x 1)/52; Q = 5567.3 coulombs; Q = I x t or t = Q/I; Time required in seconds = Q/I = 5567.3/1.25 = 4453.8 seconds
